'''Basudeb DasSarma''' (1 January 1923 – 16 November 2007) was a chemist and faculty at the [[Rajabazar Science College|University College of Science and Technology]] of the [[University of Calcutta]].  He was among an early group of Indian scholars and professionals to emigrate to the US.<ref>Indians Abroad, India Abroad (page 6), 14 May 1982</ref>  He did groundbreaking research with [[John C. Bailar Jr.]] at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], won an American Chemical Society award in 1971 <ref>American Chemical Society Award, Chemical and Engineering News (page 50), 4 October 1972</ref> for his contributions to the understanding of coordination and stereo-chemistry of metal complexes, and became a naturalized US citizen in 1972.  He was a professor of chemistry at [[West Virginia State College]] from 1966 to 1992, President of the West Virginia Academy of Science, 1981–82, and a community leader and spokesman on environmental issues<ref>Chemist Gets Silver Pen Award, Charleston Daily Mail (page 4A), 9 May 1985</ref> in the Kanawha Valley around Charleston, West Virginia. He died on 16 November 2007.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/86/i7/Obituaries.html?PageSpeed=noscript | title=Obituaries | first=Susan J.  | last=Ainsworth | work=Chemical & Engineering News | accessdate=15 October 2018 }}</ref>

== Life and career ==

=== Early life and education ===
Basudeb DasSarma was born in [[Barisal]] in [[East Bengal]] now [[Bangladesh]] on early January 1923.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=DasSarma|first1=Basudeb|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0eyNAAAAQBAJ|title=Journey of a Lifetime: Memoir of an Indian-American Chemist|last2=PhD|first2=Basudeb DasSarma|date=2010-11-09|publisher=Xlibris Corporation|isbn=978-1-4653-3424-4|language=en}}</ref> His parents were Ashutosh DasSarma, an [https://www.ayurvedanama.org/articles/2018/1/22/0c6acjnw5161xwvua1ewqu0ntf448v ayurvedic physician] (''kaviraj'') and an active [[Indian independence movement]] activist and Surabala DasSarma.<ref name=":0" /> He started his education at the early age of 4.<ref name=":0" /> His first lessons were the [[Bengali alphabet]] and was taught by his father. Later on his sister became his instructor.<ref name=":0" /> Basudeb started his first public schooling at the age of 11 in grade 4 at [[Jhalokati Government Boys High School]].<ref name=":0" /> After receiving high scores in high school, Basudeb became a student in [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[Brojomohun College]] (1940-1944).<ref name=":0" /> Since Basudeb was facing financial difficulties, he had to take private tuition to afford his housing rent during his college life.<ref name=":0" /> After Bachelors Basudeb completed his [[Master of Science]] (1944-1946) and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in [[University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture]] under the [[University of Calcutta]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=DasSarma, Basudeb {{!}} University of Illinois Archives|url=https://archon.library.illinois.edu/?p=creators/creator&id=2556|access-date=2021-04-14|website=University of Illinois Archives Holdings Database|language=en}}</ref>

=== Career ===
After completing his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] Basudeb started his career as a lecturer in chemistry in [[University of Calcutta]] (1950-1953).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> From 1953-1955 he worked as a research associate in the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] with professor of Inorganic Chemistry [[John C. Bailar Jr.]]<ref name=":3" /> The research was about learning more about coordination and stereo-chemistry of metal complexes.{{citation needed|date=April 2021}} After this he came back and served as a lecturer in the [[University of Calcutta]] for 2 more years from 1955-1957.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=ACS C&E News Obituary|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/86/i7/Obituaries.html?PageSpeed=noscript.|url-status=live|access-date=2021-04-14|website=cen.acs.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414190243/https://cen.acs.org/articles/86/i7/Obituaries.html?PageSpeed=noscript. |archive-date=14 April 2021 }}</ref> While teaching in the [[University of Calcutta]] he got the opportunity to work as the chief chemist at the [[Geological Survey of India]] and left his job at the [[University of Calcutta]].<ref name=":3" /> In 1966 Basudeb migrated to [[United States]] with his family and joined the [[West Virginia State University]] as a professor in chemistry.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /> He retired from the [[West Virginia State University]] in the year 1991 and remained as a [[professor emerita]] until 1992.<ref name=":3" /> Basudeb also served as research chemist for [[Union Carbide]] since 1966.{{citation needed|date=April 2021}} From 1971-1972 Basudeb served as the [[Certified Research Administrator]] in the [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]].{{citation needed|date=April 2021}} In 1988 he also served as the [[Project manager]] in [https://www.guidestar.org/profile/55-0653635 National Institute of Chemical Studies].{{citation needed|date=April 2021}}

=== Major accomplishments ===

* He won the [[American Chemical Society]] Award in 1971 for his research and publications on coordination and stereo-chemistry of metal complexes.{{citation needed|date=April 2021}}
* He won the [[West Virginia State University]]'s Outstanding Faculty Member of the Year award in 1973.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />
